newsitem.title: USA: Federated, Woolworth, Tiffany report strong results.
newsitem.headline: Federated, Woolworth, Tiffany report strong results.

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc. and Woolworth Corp. said Wednesday results rebounded to a profit from a loss in the first quarter, and luxury goods retailer Tiffany & Co. posted a 75 percent rise in income.
Federated, parent of Bloomingdale's, Macy's, Rich's and Stern's department stores, said it earned $24.1 million, or 12 cents a share, in the quarter.

This compared with a loss of $37.9 million, or 18 cents a share, in the first period of last year, which included costs from absorbing Broadway Stores Inc., which Federated acquired in a deal valued at $1.6 billion in 1995.

Cincinnati-based Federated's sales rose to $3.4 billion from $3.3 billion. Wall Street analysts had expected Federated to post a profit of just 9 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.

"Our first quarter performance reflects the growth of our successful private brands programme, along with strong results from our converted Broadway stores in California," said Federated Chairman Allen Questrom.
Federated's shares rose $2 to $38.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Standard & Poor's raised its rating on Federated's debt on Wednesday. The rating agency said the retailer's financial position had improved as a result of stronger earnings and market share gains.
While sales rose, the increase still was lackluster, analysts said. Meanwhile Federated chopped costs more deeply than expected, which added to the earnings rise.
Analysts said Federated will have to find ways to boost sales instead of relying on cost-cutting and acquisitions for future growth.

"I think the longer-term question for Federated is how are they going to drive sales as opportunities for acqusitions are diminishing and the opportunity for opening new stores is diminishing," said Jeffrey Stein of McDonald & Co.
Five-and-dime retailer Woolworth said it had a profit of $1 million, or 1 cent a share, compared with a loss of $22 million, or 17 cents a share, during the same period last year.
Sales fell to $1.77 million from $1.82 million last year. Woolworth had 550 fewer stores in the quarter than a year ago.
Analysts had expected the New York-based company to report a loss of 3 cents a share.

"We are pleased with the company's performance this past quarter and the continued progress we have made with all of our corporate-wide rebuilding initiatives," said Roger Farah, Woolworth's chief executive.

Woolworth has shed several unprofitable or weak retail divisions and liquidated a backlog of old inventory in a bid to boost profits. During the first quarter of last year, it recorded a $19 million loss to cover the cost of closing its 20-store Rx Place Drug Mart and disposing of other properties.
Woolworth reported earnings after the market closed. Its shares rose 62.5 cents to $22.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Tiffany said earnings soared 75 percent to $8.9 million, or 25 cents a share, in the first quarter from $5.1 million, or 15 cents a share, in the same quarter last year. Sales rose 10 percent to $199.7 million.
Analysts had forecast Tiffany would earn 19 cents a share, according to First Call.

The New York-based jeweller said international retail sales, which account for almost half of its total sales, rose by 17 percent to $95.2 million. Sales in Japan, its largest international market, rose 50 percent in local currency.
Shares of Tiffany touched a record high of $45.75 before retreating to $43.875, up 50 cents, on the New York Stock Exchange.
